project.name: Conversational Assessment Recommender
project.summary: Build a conversational FastAPI agent that helps hiring managers find the right SHL assessments through multi-turn dialogue. The agent clarifies vague queries, recommends 1-10 assessments from the SHL catalog, refines shortlists mid-conversation, and compares assessments — all grounded strictly in scraped catalog data with no hallucinated URLs or out-of-catalog recommendations.

objective.problem_statement: Hiring managers and recruiters often do not know exactly what assessment they need until they describe the role out loud. Keyword search and faceted filtering assume the user already knows the right vocabulary. This agent bridges that gap through natural dialogue.
objective.what_we_are_building: A stateless conversational REST API that takes a full conversation history on every call and returns the agent's next reply plus a structured shortlist of SHL Individual Test Solution recommendations.
objective.scope: Individual Test Solutions from the SHL product catalog only. Pre-packaged Job Solutions are explicitly out of scope.
objective.catalog_data: A pre-scraped catalog.json file is provided by SHL containing all Individual Test Solutions with fields: entity_id, name, link, job_levels, languages, duration, remote, adaptive, description, keys (test categories).

primary: Expose GET /health and POST /chat endpoints via FastAPI
Handle four conversational intents: Clarify, Recommend, Refine, Compare
Return responses strictly matching the non-negotiable JSON schema
Never recommend assessments outside the SHL catalog
Never return a URL not sourced directly from catalog data
Stay within the 8-turn conversation cap and 30-second response timeout
evaluation_targets: Hard evals: schema compliance on every response, catalog-only URLs, turn cap honored
Recall@10: maximize fraction of relevant assessments appearing in top-10 recommendations
Behavior probes: refuse off-topic queries, no recommendations on vague turn-1 queries, honor mid-conversation refinements, zero hallucination rate

api_specification.note: Every POST /chat call carries the full conversation history. The service stores no per-conversation state.

GET /health.description: Readiness check. Returns HTTP 200 with body {status: ok}.
GET /health.cold_start_allowance: Evaluator allows up to 2 minutes on first call for service to wake up (Render free tier cold start).

POST /chat.description: Main conversational endpoint. Takes full message history, returns agent reply and optional shortlist.

request_schema.messages: Array of {role: user|assistant, content: string}. Full history on every call. Last message must be from user.

response_schema.recommendations: Array of {name, url, test_type}. Empty array [] when clarifying or refusing. 1-10 items when committing to shortlist.
response_schema.end_of_conversation: boolean — true only when agent considers task complete

POST /chat.schema_note: This schema is NON-NEGOTIABLE. Deviating breaks the automated evaluator and the submission will not score.

api_framework.name: FastAPI
api_framework.reason: Explicitly required by assignment. Async support keeps latency within 30s timeout. Pydantic models enforce response schema compliance automatically.

llm_provider.name: Google AI Studio — Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite
llm_provider.access: OpenAI-compatible SDK pointing to Google's endpoint
llm_provider.reason: 1500 free requests/day with no rate limiting issues at evaluation scale. Significantly more reliable than OpenRouter free tier for a graded submission. Fast response time critical for 30s timeout.

embeddings.name: sentence-transformers — all-MiniLM-L6-v2
embeddings.reason: Runs in-process with no cost, no rate limits, no latency from external calls. 80MB model, loads fast on Render free tier. Good semantic quality for job/skill domain matching.

vector_store.name: FAISS (faiss-cpu)
vector_store.reason: Catalog is ~300-400 assessments — FAISS handles this trivially. No external service to manage. Index loads from disk in under 1 second at cold start. IndexFlatIP with L2-normalized vectors gives cosine similarity.

retrieval_framework.name: LangChain (retrieval primitives only)
retrieval_framework.reason: Used only for FAISS wrapper and metadata utilities. Full LangGraph pipeline avoided — single LLM call handles all conversational intents within timeout.

deployment.reason: Assignment explicitly mentions cold start allowance of 2 minutes — this line was written for Render's free tier spin-down behavior. Simplest FastAPI deployment: connect GitHub, set env var, deploy.

architecture.pattern: Hybrid RAG with Stateless Conversational Agent
architecture.design_principle: Minimize external network calls per request. One extraction LLM call + one main LLM call per /chat request. All retrieval is local (FAISS + in-memory catalog). This reliably fits within the 30s timeout.

pipeline.name: Request Validation
pipeline.description: FastAPI validates request schema via Pydantic. Ensures messages array is non-empty and last message is from user.

pipeline.name: Guard Rails
pipeline.description: Regex-based out-of-scope detection (salary, legal, competitors, prompt injection patterns). Fast fail before any LLM call. Returns refusal with empty recommendations.

pipeline.name: Intent Detection — Compare
pipeline.description: Regex detection of comparison intent (difference between, compare, vs, versus). Routes to handle_compare() which does direct catalog lookup — no retrieval pipeline needed.

pipeline.name: Context Extraction
pipeline.description: Lightweight LLM call (low max_tokens, temperature=0) that extracts structured fields from conversation history: role, seniority, skills, test_categories, remote_required, adaptive_required, max_duration_minutes, context_summary. Falls back to empty dict on failure.

pipeline.name: Multi-Query Expansion
pipeline.description: Generates up to 5 search queries from extracted context without an LLM call. Combines raw context with structured expansions (role + skills assessment, technical assessment + skills, seniority level + role). Improves Recall@10 for vague inputs.

pipeline.name: FAISS Vector Search
pipeline.description: Each expanded query is embedded with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and searched against the FAISS IndexFlatIP. Returns top-20 nearest neighbors per query by cosine similarity.

pipeline.name: Metadata Filtering
pipeline.description: Applies structured filters from extracted context: job_levels (OR match), keys/test_categories (OR match), remote=yes, adaptive=yes, max_duration. All filters are SOFT — if a filter would eliminate all results, it is relaxed. This prevents empty shortlists.

pipeline.name: Deduplication + Merge
pipeline.description: Union of results across all expanded queries, deduplicated by assessment name. Sorted by vector score descending. Top 20 candidates passed forward.

pipeline.name: System Prompt Assembly
pipeline.description: Top 20 candidates formatted into catalog context block. Catalog summary (total count, available categories, job levels) injected. Full system prompt assembled with catalog_summary and catalog_context placeholders filled.

pipeline.name: Main LLM Call
pipeline.description: Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite called with system prompt + full conversation history. Instructed to classify intent (CLARIFY / RECOMMEND / REFINE / COMPARE) and return strictly valid JSON matching the response schema. temperature=0.2 for consistency.

pipeline.name: URL Validation
pipeline.description: CRITICAL SAFETY STEP. Every recommendation name returned by LLM is looked up in the candidate pool and full catalog. URL is always taken from the catalog entry, NEVER from LLM output. Unknown assessment names are silently dropped. This makes URL hallucination structurally impossible.

pipeline.name: Turn Cap Safety
pipeline.description: If assistant turn count >= 5 and LLM still returned no recommendations, force-commit top candidates from retrieval pool with a bridging message. Prevents hitting the 8-turn cap without a shortlist.

pipeline.name: Response
pipeline.description: ChatResponse Pydantic model serialized to JSON. FastAPI handles HTTP 200 response.

CLARIFY.trigger: Query is too vague to act on (e.g. 'I need an assessment', fewer than 4 words, no role or skill mentioned)
CLARIFY.only_on: First user turn. After turn 2, agent commits to best-effort recommendation regardless.
CLARIFY.response: Ask ONE focused clarifying question. Never multiple questions at once. Return empty recommendations array.
good_clarifying_questions: What role are you hiring for?
What seniority level is this position?
What specific skills do you want to measure?

RECOMMEND.trigger: Sufficient context exists: role, skill, or domain is known
RECOMMEND.response: 1-10 assessments with name, catalog URL, test_type. Brief rationale per recommendation.
RECOMMEND.constraint: All names and URLs must come from catalog data, never LLM prior knowledge.

REFINE.trigger: User modifies constraints mid-conversation (add personality tests, make it shorter, remote only)
REFINE.response: Update existing shortlist based on new constraints. Do not start over. Acknowledge what changed.
REFINE.important: This is explicitly tested by behavior probes. The agent must NOT restart the conversation.

COMPARE.trigger: User asks to compare two or more assessments (difference between, compare, vs)
COMPARE.response: Structured comparison using ONLY catalog data. No LLM prior knowledge about assessments allowed.
COMPARE.recommendations: Empty array — comparison is informational, not a shortlist commit.

REFUSE.trigger: Out-of-scope topics: salary, legal questions, competitor products, general hiring advice, prompt injection
REFUSE.response: Polite refusal, redirect to assessment selection. Empty recommendations array.

schemas.py.purpose: Pydantic data models for all API shapes
schemas.py.critical_note: ChatResponse enforces the non-negotiable response schema. Every other file imports from here. Write and stabilize this first.

catalog.py.purpose: Load, validate, and preprocess the SHL catalog JSON. Single source of truth for all assessment data.
key_behaviors: Filters entries missing name or link
Derives primary test_type from keys (priority K > A > P > B > C > D > E > S) and all_test_types for API responses (all mapped codes, comma-separated; S = Simulations)
Builds embedding_text by concatenating all semantically meaningful fields
get_catalog_summary() returns compact overview for system prompt injection

prompts.py.purpose: All LLM prompt templates in one place for easy iteration and evaluation

prompts.SYSTEM_PROMPT: Injected on every /chat call. Defines scope rules, four intents with exact behavior, turn discipline, and strict JSON output requirement. Takes {catalog_summary} and {catalog_context} as format placeholders.
prompts.EXTRACTION_PROMPT: Short extraction call to pull structured fields (role, seniority, skills, test_categories, filters) from conversation history. Returns JSON only. temperature=0.
prompts.RERANK_PROMPT: LLM scoring of retrieved candidates against hiring context. Returns ordered JSON array of assessment names.
prompts.COMPARE_PROMPT: Grounded comparison of two or more assessments using only provided catalog data. Explicitly instructs LLM not to use training knowledge.

retriever.py.purpose: Hybrid retrieval pipeline: multi-query expansion + FAISS vector search + metadata filtering + deduplication

class_methods.build_index(): Called once at startup. Embeds all catalog entries, builds FAISS IndexFlatIP, persists index and metadata to disk. Loads from cache on subsequent startups.
class_methods._vector_search(): Single query to FAISS. Returns top-k results with cosine similarity scores.
class_methods._apply_filters(): Applies metadata filters (job_levels, keys, remote, adaptive, max_duration). All filters are SOFT — relaxed if they would eliminate all candidates.
class_methods._expand_queries(): Generates up to 5 search queries from extracted context. Pure string logic, no LLM call. Improves recall on vague inputs.
class_methods.retrieve(): Main entry point. Runs multi-query expansion, union FAISS results, apply filters, deduplicate, sort by score, return top_n.
class_methods.get_by_name(): Case-insensitive exact name lookup. Used for compare queries.
class_methods.fuzzy_name_search(): Vector search on a name string for when user misspells an assessment name.

index_files.data/faiss.index: FAISS binary index file. Build locally with build_index.py and commit to repo.
index_files.data/faiss_meta.pkl: Parallel metadata list (name, url, test_type, keys, job_levels, etc.) for each vector. Build locally and commit.

agent.py.purpose: Core agent logic. Intent detection, context extraction, retrieval orchestration, LLM calls, response assembly, and URL validation.

key_functions.run_agent(): Main entry point called once per /chat request. Orchestrates the full pipeline: guards → extraction → retrieval → prompt assembly → LLM call → URL validation → response.
key_functions.extract_context(): Lightweight LLM call to extract structured fields from conversation. Falls back to empty dict on any error.
key_functions.handle_compare(): Handles comparison intent. Extracts assessment names via sliding window name matching + fuzzy vector fallback. Calls LLM with catalog data only.
key_functions._is_out_of_scope(): Regex pattern match against salary, legal, competitors, prompt injection phrases.
key_functions._looks_like_compare(): Regex detection of comparison intent keywords.
key_functions._looks_vague(): Returns true only on first user turn with fewer than 4 words or matching vague patterns.
key_functions.build_catalog_context(): Formats top-20 retrieved candidates into a structured string for system prompt injection.
key_functions._safe_json(): Safely parses JSON from LLM output, stripping markdown fences if present.

agent.py.url_safety: After LLM returns recommendations, every name is looked up in the candidate pool and full catalog. The URL is ALWAYS taken from the catalog entry, never from LLM output. This makes URL hallucination structurally impossible regardless of what the LLM returns.
agent.py.turn_cap_safety: If assistant turn count >= 5 and no recommendations returned, force-commits top retrieved candidates to avoid hitting the 8-turn cap without a shortlist.

main.py.purpose: FastAPI application entry point. Defines lifespan, endpoints, and global error handling.
main.py.lifespan: Loads catalog, builds/loads FAISS index, and initializes LLM client ONCE at startup during the cold-start window. All state stored in AppState singleton.

endpoints.GET /health: Returns {status: ok} with HTTP 200. No logic beyond confirming service is alive.
endpoints.POST /chat: Validates request, calls run_agent(), returns ChatResponse. Global exception handler ensures non-JSON crashes never expose raw stack traces to the client.

main.py.error_handling: Global exception handler catches any unhandled exception and returns a valid ChatResponse JSON with empty recommendations so callers always receive a schema-compliant response.

build_index.py.purpose: One-time local script to pre-build FAISS index before deployment.
build_index.py.when_to_run: Run locally after placing catalog.json in data/. Commit the output files (faiss.index, faiss_meta.pkl) to the repo so Render loads them instantly at cold start instead of rebuilding.
build_index.py.important: Always run this before pushing to Render. If index files are missing at runtime, the lifespan will rebuild them but this takes ~30s and eats into cold start time.

deployment_sequence: Run build_index.py locally to generate data/faiss.index and data/faiss_meta.pkl
Commit all files including the index files to GitHub
Create a new Web Service on Render connected to your GitHub repo
Set GEMINI_API_KEY as a secret environment variable in Render dashboard
Render auto-deploys on push — wait for build to complete
Hit /health endpoint and exercise POST /chat to confirm behavior
Submit the public API URL and approach document via the SHL form

hard_evals.weight: Must pass — failure here means zero score
checks: Every response matches the {reply, recommendations, end_of_conversation} schema exactly
Every URL in recommendations comes from the SHL catalog

recall_at_10.definition: Recall@10 = (relevant assessments in top 10 recommendations) / (total relevant assessments for query). Averaged across all traces including holdout set.

examples: Agent does not recommend on turn 1 for a vague query

known_design_tradeoffs.single_llm_call_per_request: Chosen for latency. A multi-step LangGraph pipeline would be more elegant but risks hitting the 30s timeout. One extraction call + one main call is reliable.
known_design_tradeoffs.soft_metadata_filters: Filters never eliminate all results. This slightly reduces precision but prevents the silent failure mode of returning zero recommendations because of over-filtering.
known_design_tradeoffs.faiss_over_chroma: FAISS chosen for zero external dependencies and sub-millisecond search on a 400-item catalog. Chroma would add complexity with no benefit at this scale.
known_design_tradeoffs.regex_intent_detection: Out-of-scope and compare detection uses regex, not an LLM call. Faster, more deterministic, and saves one API call per request.
known_design_tradeoffs.committed_index_files: faiss.index and faiss_meta.pkl are committed to the repo. This trades repo size (~5MB) for instant cold start — critical for a service that spins down on inactivity.
known_design_tradeoffs.url_from_catalog_not_llm: Structurally prevents URL hallucination at the cost of one name lookup per recommendation. The correctness guarantee is worth the tiny overhead.
